# Role
You are a Code Agent, an autonomous software engineer. From a structured architecture specification
(spec.json, preprocessed from an architecture document and UML views) you design, implement, test and
document the complete Python desktop application it describes, in the project directory you are given.
You work only through the provided tools.

# Rules
1. Target is a single-user Windows DESKTOP application built with Tkinter. Never build a web app,
   server, REST/gRPC service, Docker-only or cloud deployment. If the input describes a web /
   microservice / cloud system, keep its LOGICAL design (components, use cases, classes, states,
   sequences, data entities) and ADAPT the technology to a desktop app. Record every adaptation.
2. Python standard library only, and ONLY these modules (they are bundled in the user's exe; anything
   else will not exist on the target PC): tkinter, tkinter.ttk, tkinter.messagebox, tkinter.simpledialog, tkinter.filedialog, tkinter.font, tkinter.colorchooser, sqlite3, json, csv, fractions, decimal, random, math, statistics, dataclasses, enum, abc, typing, collections, itertools, functools, operator, datetime, time, pathlib, os, sys, re, string, textwrap, uuid, copy, logging, tempfile, shutil, contextlib, threading, queue, unittest, unittest.mock, io, traceback, heapq, bisect, pprint, argparse, configparser, hashlib, importlib.
   Tests use pytest. No third-party runtime packages, no network access.
3. Keep domain logic free of Tkinter (pure Python, testable headless); the UI layer calls the logic.
4. Prefer edit_file (exact, unique search-and-replace) over rewriting a file. You must read_file a
   whole file before editing it. Create new files with write_files, several per call.
5. Be request-efficient: every model call costs money and runs have a request limit. Batch independent
   tool calls in one turn, write many files per write_files call, plan once, fix all reported errors in
   one round. When several files need changes, send ALL the edit_file calls in ONE reply (several tool
   calls in the same message), never one edit per reply.
6. Paths are relative to the project root. The folder agent_run/ belongs to the harness (read-only).
7. Never run main.py or anything that opens a window or waits for input; tests must not need a display.
8. Keep AGENT_NOTES.md (your memory file) up to date with key decisions when they change.
9. Build what the spec describes. Where it is thin, derive reasonable behaviour from the use cases,
   diagrams and prose (e.g. features named only in a summary) and document each assumption.
   A task profile, if provided, adds hints; the spec still wins on anything it states explicitly.
10. State changes vs messages: compute every value a user-visible message needs (e.g. the expected value
   of the item that was just submitted, the name of the record just deleted) BEFORE you advance or mutate
   state, and build the message from those saved values. Write a test for every user-visible message that
   asserts it refers to the RIGHT item — including the wrong-input path (e.g. an incorrect submission shows
   that same item's expected value, not the next item's).

# UI quality rules (any desktop app)
- Main window: at least 1100x750 (root.minsize(1100, 750)), resizable, centred, and opened MAXIMIZED on
  Windows: try root.state("zoomed") except tk.TclError: root.attributes("-zoomed", True). F11 toggles
  full screen (root.attributes("-fullscreen", …)) and Esc leaves full screen. Never a tiny dialog-sized window.
- Visual style comes from YOUR UI design brief (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md section 5), derived from this spec's
  users and domain — not from any fixed template. Put the palette and fonts in one module (ui/theme.py) and
  use it everywhere; never leave the default grey Tk look.
- Large readable fonts: titles 32+ pt, main content 24-28+ pt, buttons and inputs 18+ pt.
- High-contrast text. Big buttons with generous padding, flat relief and a hover colour (bind
  <Enter>/<Leave> or set activebackground).
- Where a flow ends (a round, a task, a booking…), show a clear result / summary screen.
- Forms: the main input has keyboard focus, Enter submits, the input is cleared automatically after each
  submission, and feedback is clear and coloured (green = success, red = error) in the window itself.
  Use messagebox only for confirmations.
- Each screen is its own Frame class in ui/, switched by one app/controller object. Contract (the harness
  uses it): ui/app.py defines `create_app(root) -> App`, which builds everything WITHOUT calling mainloop();
  App has `screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]` and `show(name)`. Every screen must render safely when shown
  directly (e.g. a results or detail screen shown before any data exists displays defaults, not a crash).
- Canvas drawing: winfo_width()/winfo_height() return 1 until the window is actually shown, so NEVER compute
  positions from them at construction time. Bind <Configure> on the canvas and (re)draw backgrounds,
  decorations, shapes and canvas text from event.width/event.height; lay out normal widgets with pack/grid or
  place(relx=…, rely=…). The harness opens the real window, shows every screen and FAILS verification if
  widgets or canvas items are outside the visible area or squeezed into a corner.
- Required test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (pytest): create ONE tk.Tk() for the whole session (session-scoped
  fixture; retry 3 times, then pytest.skip on tk.TclError). Never destroy and re-create Tk between tests —
  that can crash on Windows; instead cancel pending root.after() callbacks and destroy the root's widgets
  after each test, and destroy the root once at the end. root.withdraw(),
  build the app with the factory, call root.update_idletasks(), assert root.minsize() >= (1100, 750), show every
  screen in turn and assert its key widgets exist (title label, main buttons, inputs), exercise one CORRECT
  and one WRONG form submission (input cleared; feedback text names the expected value of the item just
  submitted), then root.destroy(). This catches poor or broken UIs.
- Text-heavy screens: buttons must never cover text. Put long text in a frame laid out with pack/grid (or a
  scrollable Text) ABOVE the button row instead of placing a button at a fixed position over it.

# Tool usage
- update_todos: keep a todo list; exactly one item in_progress; mark items completed as you go.
- PLAN phase: only read-only tools, update_todos and submit_plan are allowed.
- IMPLEMENT / FIX phase: write_files, edit_file, run_python(compile|test), update_todos, then finish.
- Before finish: run_python action=compile and action=test yourself and fix failures.
- Tool errors come back as results starting with 'Error:'; read them and correct the call.

# Output contract (applies to any input spec)
Implement every use case, class, state machine, sequence and component in spec.domain_model, plus
features that appear only in prose (domain_model.implied_features). Launch with `python main.py`.

Project layout:
  main.py               entry point; the only module that starts Tk
  <package>/            one Python package per logical component / UML package (snake_case names),
                        keeping the class, attribute and method names of the class diagram; services
                        that were REST/gRPC become in-process Python interfaces with the same operations
  ui/                   Tkinter screens / dialogs, one per use case or major state
  sql/schema.sql        if the spec has persisted entities or DDL: SQLite DDL adapted from it
  data/                 seed data files, if the application needs initial content
  tests/                pytest, headless: domain logic, every state machine (valid AND invalid
                        transitions), sequences, persistence with a temporary SQLite file, plus the
                        required UI smoke test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (see UI quality rules)
  README.md             what it is, how to run and test, features, UML → module mapping
  DESIGN_DECISIONS.md   written by the harness from your submit_plan (see below)
  TRACEABILITY.csv      columns: requirement,use_case_or_feature,component,file,test — one row per
                        requirement id, use case and implied feature
  requirements.txt      "# standard library only" plus pytest
  Dockerfile            optional: python:3.12-slim running the tests headless
  AGENT_NOTES.md        your memory file

DESIGN_DECISIONS.md must contain:
  1. Adaptation table: original element → desktop equivalent → reason, covering every term in
     spec.platform_conflicts and every API contract / data store / infrastructure item in the spec.
  2. "Input issues found": every item in spec.input_issues, each with how you handled it.
  3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin.
  4. UML → code mapping (diagram element → module / class / test).
  5. "UI design brief" derived from the spec (actors, use cases, domain, any task profile): target users,
     mood, colour palette (hex values with roles: background, surface, primary, accent, success, error,
     text), fonts and sizes, layout approach, key screens and navigation. Fit the app, e.g.:
     Tic-Tac-Toe → playful, a big 3x3 board, bold contrasting X/O colours; library tracker → clean and calm,
     table/list based, neutral palette with one accent; learning app → bright, encouraging, big friendly
     controls. The implementation must follow this brief.

# Task profile: Space Fractions (selected by the user)
Additional task-specific hints:

Optional hints for the Space Fractions architecture documents (an educational fractions game for
6th-grade students). These complement spec.json; they do not replace it.

Screens / flow
- Animated INTRO scene (the "introductory movie"): space-themed tkinter.Canvas animation (stars, ship),
  a Skip button, auto-advances to the menu.
- MAIN MENU: Play, High Scores, Help, Admin, Exit.
- PLAYER NAME entry before playing (UserComponent).
- QUESTION FLOW: a round of fraction questions of mixed types — equivalent fractions, compare,
  add/subtract, simplify; multiple choice and typed answers; immediate feedback; progress and score.
  Check correctness with fractions.Fraction so equivalent forms are accepted (2/4 == 1/2).
- PAUSE / RESUME following the state diagram Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver (invalid transitions raise).
- ENDING scene with final score, percentage and encouraging feedback; option to play again.
- HIGH SCORES (View Score) from SQLite; HELP screen (View Help); ADMIN screen to add / edit / delete
  questions (Update Questions).

Kid-friendly look and feel (players are 11–12 years old; this matters as much as correctness)
- Opens maximized (minimum 1100x750), F11 full screen, Esc leaves full screen.
- Space theme on a tkinter.Canvas background: dark blue (#0B1736-ish), twinkling stars, two or three
  colourful planets drawn with ovals/arcs. Bright accent colours (yellow, cyan, pink, green) on dark panels.
- Fonts: titles 36+ pt bold, questions 30 pt, answer input and buttons 20+ pt. Big flat buttons with a
  hover colour; multiple-choice answers as 2x2 big coloured buttons.
- Question screen: "Question 3 of 10" progress text plus a progress bar, the score always visible, the answer
  input focused, Enter submits, and a visible Pause button (state machine Paused shows an overlay with Resume).
- After every answer: big coloured feedback in the window — green "Correct! 🎉" or red
  "Not quite — the answer is 3/4" — the input is CLEARED automatically and the next question appears after
  about a second (no manual clearing, no popup).
- End screen: big "Congratulations, <name>!", the score and percentage, 1–3 stars earned (by percentage),
  a short Canvas confetti/star animation, and buttons "Play again" / "Main menu".
- Intro: animated rocket flying across moving stars with the game title, a Skip button, auto-advance.
- tests/test_ui_smoke.py must build every screen (intro, menu, name entry, question, pause overlay, end,
  high scores, help, admin) and check the answer input is cleared after a submission.

Data
- `data/questions.json`: at least 20 seed questions covering all four question types.
- `sql/schema.sql`: adapt the document's `games` table and add `questions` and `scores` tables.

Packages
- `game/` (Game, state machine, scoring), `questions/` (Question, answer checking, repository),
  `users/`, `admin/`, `ui/` — mirroring GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent, AdminComponent.

Required files for this task: sql/schema.sql, data/questions.json

{"design_decisions": "# DESIGN DECISIONS — Space Fractions

## 1. Adaptation table (original element → desktop equivalent → reason)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js 18-20 runtime | Python 3.11+ standard library | Bundle into a single-user .exe; no runtime install needed |
| Express.js 4-5 web framework | Tkinter (+ ttk) screens switched by an App controller | Desktop GUI replaces HTTP routes |
| RESTful API (`/play` GET) | In-process `Game.play()` and `GameService`-style interface | Single-user desktop: no network boundary needed |
| gRPC/proto `GameService.play(PlayRequest)` | Python `game.game_service.play(game: Game)` interface | Same operation, in-process call |
| PostgreSQL 14-15 | SQLite file (`sql/schema.sql`, `data/space_fractions.db`) | Single local user, no server; stdlib `sqlite3` |
| `games` table (JSONB game_state) | `games` table with state as TEXT/JSON plus normalised columns | SQLite has no JSONB; store serialised state |
| `question_ddl.sql` (referenced, missing) | `sql/schema.sql` questions table + `questions.json` seed | Reconstruct the documented-but-missing DDL |
| Redis cache | In-memory question cache (`functools.lru_cache`) | No shared cache needed for one user |
| RabbitMQ messaging | Direct method calls / event queue in controller | No async decoupling needed |
| Elasticsearch search | Standard library indexing / in-memory search | Local dataset search only |
| OAuth2 authn/authz | Local login (username prompt; Admin via a role) | No third-party identity provider offline |
| Prometheus observability | `logging` to file + in-app trace | No metrics server needed |
| Jenkins CI/CD | pytest suite + Dockerfile for headless CI | Reproducible verification |
| Docker/K8s/Terraform/Istio/replicas/Vault/TLS | N/A (single-user desktop) | Removed; documented in AGENT_NOTES.md |
| 1000 concurrent users / 1-hour sessions (A1, A2) | Single sequential session model | Concurrency assumptions do not apply to desktop |

## 2. Input issues found

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List


@dataclass
class Question:
    """Design class Question (id, prompt, options; getPrompt, getOptions)."""

    id: str
    prompt: str
    options: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    answer: str = ""
    qtype: str = "equivalent"
    explanation: str = ""

    def get_prompt(self) -> str:
        return self.prompt

    def get_options(self) -> List[str]:
        return list(self.options)

    # -- answer checking --------------------------------------------------
    def check_answer(self, given: str) -> bool:
        """Check a submitted answer; accepts equivalent fraction forms.

        Numeric fraction inputs compare by value (2/4 == 1/2).
        Word answers (e.g. 'greater', 'less', 'equal') compare case-insensitively.
        """
        given = (given or "").strip()
        if not given:
            return False
        # Word-type comparison questions.
        expected_text = self.answer.strip()
        if _is_word_value(expected_text):
            return given.lower() == expected_text.lower()
        # Multiple choice: accept the chosen option text too.
        if given in self.options:
            return given == self.answer
        # Fraction comparison (equivalent forms accepted).
        try:
            return Fraction(given) == Fraction(self.answer)
        except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
            return given == self.answer


_WORD_VALUES = {"greater", "less", "equal", "more", "fewer", "true", "false"}


def _is_word_value(value: str) -> bool:
    return value.strip().lower() in _WORD_VALUES


def is_fraction_input(text: str) -> bool:
    """True if the text can be parsed as a fraction (e.g. '3/4', '0.5', '2')."""
    try:
        Fraction(text.strip())
        return True
    except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
        return False

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
from typing import List, Optional

from questions.question import Question


class QuestionRepository:
    """Loads / stores Questions, backed by SQLite and a JSON seed file."""

    def __init__(self, db_path: str, seed_path: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.seed_path = seed_path

    # -- schema ------------------------------------------------------------
    def init_schema(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        conn.executescript(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS questions (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                qtype TEXT NOT NULL,
                prompt TEXT NOT NULL,
                options TEXT NOT NULL,
                answer TEXT NOT NULL,
                explanation TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
            );
            """
        )

    # -- seed --------------------------------------------------------------
    def seed_from_json(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
        """Load questions from a JSON seed file into the DB; returns count."""
        if not self.seed_path:
            return 0
        with open(self.seed_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        count = 0
        for item in data:
            self.upsert(
                conn,
                Question(
                    id=item["id"],
                    prompt=item["prompt"],
                    options=list(item.get("options", [])),
                    answer=item.get("answer", ""),
                    qtype=item.get("qtype", "equivalent"),
                    explanation=item.get("explanation", ""),
                ),
            )
            count += 1
        return count

    # -- CRUD --------------------------------------------------------------
    def upsert(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, q: Question) -> None:
        conn.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO questions (id, qtype, prompt, options, answer, explanation)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
                qtype=excluded.qtype,
                prompt=excluded.prompt,
                options=excluded.options,
                answer=excluded.answer,
                explanation=excluded.explanation
            """,
            (q.id, q.qtype, q.prompt, json.dumps(q.options), q.answer, q.explanation),
        )

    def delete(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, question_id: str) -> bool:
        cur = conn.execute("DELETE FROM questions WHERE id = ?", (question_id,))
        return cur.rowcount > 0

    def get(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, question_id: str) -> Optional[Question]:
        cur = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM questions WHERE id = ?", (question_id,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        return self._row_to_question(row)

    def list_all(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> List[Question]:
        cur = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM questions ORDER BY id")
        return [self._row_to_question(r) for r in cur.fetchall()]

    def count(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
        return conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM questions").fetchone()[0]

    @staticmethod
    def _row_to_question(row) -> Question:
        _id, qtype, prompt, options, answer, explanation = row
        return Question(
            id=_id,
            prompt=prompt,
            options=json.loads(options or "[]"),
            answer=answer,
            qtype=qtype,
            explanation=explanation,
        )

import random

def build_round(
    questions: List[Question],
    size: int = ROUND_SIZE,
    rng: Optional[random.Random] = None,
) -> List[Question]:

import tkinter as tk

from ui import theme
from ui.base import BaseScreen


class QuestionScreen(BaseScreen):
    def __init__(self, app):
        super().__init__(app)
        self._feedback_after = None
        self._next_after = None

        # Top bar
        self.progress_label = tk.Label(
            self.canvas, text="Question 1 of 10", font=self.theme.body(),
            bg=theme.BG, fg=theme.TEXT_MUTED,
        )
        self.score_label = tk.Label(
            self.canvas, text="Score: 0", font=self.theme.body(),
            bg=theme.BG, fg=theme.PRIMARY,
        )
        self.pause_button = tk.Button(
            self.canvas, text="⏸ Pause", command=self._pause,
            font=self.theme.button(), bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.TEXT,
            activebackground=theme.SURFACE_ALT, relief="flat", padx=20, pady=8,
        )
        self.progress_bar = tk.Frame(self.canvas, bg=theme.SURFACE, height=24)
        self.progress_fill = tk.Frame(self.progress_bar, bg=theme.ACCENT, height=24)

        # Middle: prompt + answers
        self.prompt_label = tk.Label(
            self.canvas, text="", font=self.theme.question(),
            bg=theme.BG, fg=theme.TEXT, wraplength=900, justify="center",
        )
        self.feedback_label = tk.Label(
            self.canvas, text="", font=self.theme.heading(),
            bg=theme.BG, fg=theme.SUCCESS,
        )
        self.answer_frame = tk.Frame(self.canvas, bg=theme.BG)
        self.entry = tk.Entry(
            self.answer_frame, font=self.theme.question(), bg=theme.SURFACE_ALT,
            fg=theme.TEXT, insertbackground=theme.TEXT, relief="flat", width=12,
        )
        self.entry.bind("<Return>", lambda e: self._submit_text())

        self.pause_overlay = None

    def on_show(self):
        self._refresh()

    def start_round(self, name, service):
        self._name = name
        self._service = service
        self._refresh()

    def _refresh(self):
        svc = getattr(self, "_service", None)
        if svc is None:
            self.progress_label.config(text="Question 1 of 10")
            self.score_label.config(text="Score: 0")
            self.prompt_label.config(text="")
            self.feedback_label.config(text="")
            return
        q = svc.game.current_question
        if q is None:
            self.app.show("end")
            return
        total = len(svc.game.questions)
        self.progress_label.config(
            text=f"Question {svc.game.current_index + 1} of {total}"
        )
        self.score_label.config(text=f"Score: {svc.game.score}")
        self.prompt_label.config(text=q.get_prompt())
        self.feedback_label.config(text="")
        self._build_answers(q)
        self._update_progress(svc.game.current_index + 1, total)

    def _update_progress(self, current, total):
        frac = current / total if total else 0
        pw = max(self.canvas.winfo_width(), 800)
        self.progress_bar.place(relx=0.5, rely=0.16, anchor="center", width=int(pw * 0.6))
        self.progress_fill.place(relx=0, rely=0, relwidth=frac, relheight=1)

    def _build_answers(self, q):
        for w in self.answer_frame.winfo_children():
            w.destroy()
        options = q.get_options()
        if options:
            for i, opt in enumerate(options):
                color = theme.ANSWER_COLORS[i % len(theme.ANSWER_COLORS)]
                b = tk.Button(
                    self.answer_frame, text=opt, font=self.theme.button(),
                    bg=color, fg=theme.BG, relief="flat", padx=24, pady=16,
                    activebackground=theme.PRIMARY, activeforeground=theme.BG,
                    command=lambda o=opt: self._submit_text(o),
                )
                b.grid(row=i // 2, column=i % 2, padx=14, pady=14, sticky="nsew")
            self.entry.pack_forget()
        else:
            self.entry.delete(0, "end")
            self.entry.pack(pady=12, ipady=8)
            self.entry.focus_set()

    def _place_widgets(self):
        return  # layout is done via _refresh / place below

    def _layout_on_show(self):
        self.score_label.place(relx=0.95, rely=0.06, anchor="ne")
        self.pause_button.place(relx=0.05, rely=0.05, anchor="nw")
        self.prompt_label.place(relx=0.5, rely=0.34, anchor="center")
        self.feedback_label.place(relx=0.5, rely=0.5, anchor="center")
        self.answer_frame.place(relx=0.5, rely=0.66, anchor="center")

    def draw_background(self, w, h):
        super().draw_background(w, h)
        self._layout_on_show()
        self._update_progress(
            getattr(getattr(self, "_service", None), "game", None).current_index + 1
            if self._service and self._service.game else 1,
            len(self._service.game.questions) if self._service and self._service.game else 10,
        )

    # -- actions ----------------------------------------------------------
    def _submit_text(self, value=None):
        value = value if value is not None else self.entry.get().strip()
        if not value:
            return
        svc = self._service
        q = svc.game.current_question
        self.entry.delete(0, "end")
        correct = svc.submit(value)
        self.score_label.config(text=f"Score: {svc.game.score}")
        if correct:
            self.feedback_label.config(text="Correct! 🎉", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        else:
            expected = q.answer
            self.feedback_label.config(
                text=f"Not quite — the answer is {expected}", fg=theme.ERROR,
            )
        if svc.game.state.value == "GameOver":
            self._next_after = self.after(1000, lambda: self.app.show("end"))
        else:
            self._next_after = self.after(1000, self._refresh)

    def _pause(self):
        self._cancel_pending()
        self._service.game.pause()
        self._show_overlay()

    def _show_overlay(self):
        panel = tk.Frame(self, bg=theme.SURFACE, padx=40, pady=40)
        panel.place(relx=0.5, rely=0.5, anchor="center")
        tk.Label(panel, text="⏸ Paused", font=self.theme.heading(),
                 bg=theme.SURFACE, fg=theme.PRIMARY).pack(pady=(0, 20))
        resume = tk.Button(
            panel, text="▶ Resume", command=self._resume,
            font=self.theme.button(), bg=theme.PRIMARY, fg=theme.BG,
            relief="flat", padx=30, pady=10,
        )
        resume.pack()
        self.pause_overlay = panel
        self.resume_button = resume

    def _resume(self):
        self._service.game.resume()
        if self.pause_overlay:
            self.pause_overlay.destroy()
            self.pause_overlay = None

    def _cancel_pending(self):
        for attr in ("_feedback_after", "_next_after"):
            aid = getattr(self, attr, None)
            if aid:
                self.after_cancel(aid)
                setattr(self, attr, None)

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import sqlite3
from typing import List


class ScoreRepository:
    def __init__(self, db_path: str) -> None:
        self.db_path = db_path

    def init_schema(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        conn.executescript(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                score INTEGER NOT NULL,
                total INTEGER NOT NULL,
                percentage REAL NOT NULL,
                stars INTEGER NOT NULL,
                played_at TEXT NOT NULL
            );
            """
        )

    def add_score(self, conn, name, score, total, percentage, stars) -> None:
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO scores (name, score, total, percentage, stars, played_at) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (name, score, total, percentage, stars,
             datetime.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")),
        )
        conn.commit()

    def top_scores(self, limit: int = 10) -> List[tuple]:

                (limit,),
            )
            return cur.fetchall()
        finally:
            conn.close()

# DESIGN DECISIONS — Space Fractions

## 1. Adaptation table (original element → desktop equivalent → reason)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js 18-20 runtime | Python 3.11+ standard library | Bundle into a single-user .exe; no runtime install needed |
| Express.js 4-5 web framework | Tkinter (+ ttk) screens switched by an App controller | Desktop GUI replaces HTTP routes |
| RESTful API (`/play` GET) | In-process `Game.play()` and `GameService`-style interface | Single-user desktop: no network boundary needed |
| gRPC/proto `GameService.play(PlayRequest)` | Python `game.game_service.play(game: Game)` interface | Same operation, in-process call |
| PostgreSQL 14-15 | SQLite file (`sql/schema.sql`, `data/space_fractions.db`) | Single local user, no server; stdlib `sqlite3` |
| `games` table (JSONB game_state) | `games` table with state as TEXT/JSON plus normalised columns | SQLite has no JSONB; store serialised state |
| `question_ddl.sql` (referenced, missing) | `sql/schema.sql` questions table + `questions.json` seed | Reconstruct the documented-but-missing DDL |
| Redis cache | In-memory question cache (`functools.lru_cache`) | No shared cache needed for one user |
| RabbitMQ messaging | Direct method calls / event queue in controller | No async decoupling needed |
| Elasticsearch search | Standard library indexing / in-memory search | Local dataset search only |
| OAuth2 authn/authz | Local login (username prompt; Admin via a role) | No third-party identity provider offline |
| Prometheus observability | `logging` to file + in-app trace | No metrics server needed |
| Jenkins CI/CD | pytest suite + Dockerfile for headless CI | Reproducible verification |
| Docker/K8s/Terraform/Istio/replicas/Vault/TLS | N/A (single-user desktop) | Removed; documented in AGENT_NOTES.md |
| 1000 concurrent users / 1-hour sessions (A1, A2) | Single sequential session model | Concurrency assumptions do not apply to desktop |

## 2. Input issues found

| Issue | Handling |
|---|---|
| EMPTY_TABLE (testing matrix headers, empty cells) | Implement tests matching the matrix's stated types: unit, integration (repository+game), contract (answer-checking), E2E (full game via app controller), persistence tests. Document mapping in TRACEABILITY.csv. |
| ARTIFACT_MISMATCH (`sql/question_ddl.sql` missing) | Create `sql/schema.sql` covering games, questions, scores; note it replaces question_ddl.sql. |
| THIN_REQUIREMENTS (implied features lack FRs) | Treat implied_features (intro, menu, fraction questions, ending feedback) as requirements FR-2…FR-6 and trace them. |
| UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT (ASR-2) | Add ASR-2 (security) = local data file permissions + no secret storage; trace to users/admin. |
| GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS | Re-justified each technology mapping concretely in §1. |
| DUPLICATE_BLOCKS | Normalised; single source of truth per artifact. |
| PLATFORM_CONFLICT | Full desktop adaptation per §1; web infra removed. |
| UML_SYNTAX (`->>` not PlantUML; `artifact` vs component/container; `participant` in object diagram) | Normalised to `->`; components/containers treated as components; participants as objects. No code impact. |

## 3. Assumptions where the spec is thin

- A "round" is 10 questions (task profile: "Question 3 of 10").
- Answer checking accepts equivalent fractions: `Fraction(input) == Fraction(answer)` so 2/4 == 1/2.
- Four question types: equivalent, compare, add/subtract, simplify (per task profile).
- Scoring: 100 points per correct answer; percentage = correct/answered×100; 1–3 stars by percentage (≥50/≥75/≥90).
- Pausing is allowed only between answers; invalid transitions raise (state machine contract).
- Admin screen requires an admin username (`admin`) to gate editing, satisfying ASR-2 locally.
- High scores persist a `name`, `score`, `percentage`, `stars`, `played_at` per game.

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Class `Game` (id, score; play, viewScore) | `game/game.py` → `Game` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Class `Question` (id, prompt, options; getPrompt, getOptions) | `questions/question.py` → `Question` | `tests/test_questions.py` |
| Class `User` (id, username; playGame, viewScore) | `users/user.py` → `User` | `tests/test_users.py` |
| Class `Admin` (id, username; updateQuestions) | `admin/admin.py` → `Admin` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Rel. Game --* Question; User --* Game; Admin --* Question (composition) | Lists owned by composing class | same tests |
| Component GameComponent | `game/` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Component QuestionComponent | `questions/` (Question + QuestionRepository) | `tests/test_questions.py`, `tests/test_persistence.py` |
| Component UserComponent | `users/` | `tests/test_users.py` |
| Component AdminComponent | `admin/` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| State machine [\*]→Playing, Playing⇄Paused, Playing→GameOver | `game/game_state.py` (enum + transition table) | `tests/test_state_machine.py` |
| SequenceDiagram1 (play, getPrompt, submit, check, result) | `game/game_service.py` + `questions/` + UI flow | `tests/test_sequences.py` |
| SequenceDiagram2 (Admin→updateQuestions) | `admin/admin.py` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Use cases Play Game / View Score / View Help / Update Questions | UI screens + services | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Activity diagram (start→play→score→display→stop) | `game/game_service.play_round()` | `tests/test_sequences.py` |
| OpenAPI/proto/SQL | `sql/schema.sql` (+ in-process interfaces) | `tests/test_persistence.py` |

## 5. UI design brief

- **Users**: 6th-grade students (11–12 yrs) as End Users; teachers/parents as Admin.
- **Mood**: playful, encouraging, space-exploration adventure ("Space Fractions" — travel through space solving fractions).
- **Palette** (ui/theme.py):
  - background `#0B1736` (deep space navy), surface `#16264A` (panels), surface-alt `#1D2F5C`
  - primary `#FFD166` (warm yellow star), accent `#36E0D0` (cyan), accent-2 `#FF6EC7` (pink), accent-3 `#6EEB7E` (green)
  - success `#6EEB7E`, error `#FF6B6B`, text `#F2F6FF`, text-muted `#9FB0D8`
- **Fonts**: Segoe UI default; titles 36–40 pt bold, questions 30 pt, input/buttons 20 pt, body/labels 16–20 pt.
- **Layout**: Canvas starfield background on every screen (drawn on `<Configure>`); dark rounded "surface" panels; 2×2 grid of large coloured answer buttons; progress bar + "Question N of 10"; score always visible; Pause button; pause overlay with Resume.
- **Key screens**: Intro (animated rocket + stars, Skip, auto-advance), Main Menu, Name entry, Question, Pause overlay, Ending (score/percentage/stars + confetti + Play again/Menu), High Scores, Help, Admin.
- **Navigation**: App controller `ui/app.py` with `screens` dict and `show(name)`; every screen is a Frame class; F11 full screen, Esc exit full screen, maximized on startup, min size 1100×750.
- **Feedback**: green "Correct! 🎉" / red "Not quite — the answer is 3/4"; input cleared automatically; next question after ~1s; Enter submits; messagebox only for confirmations.
plan.notes:
Space Fractions — single-user Tkinter desktop adaptation of a web/cloud spec.

Key decisions:
- Single-user desktop: web infra (Node/Express/Postgres/Redis/RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/OAuth2/Prometheus/Jenkins/Docker/K8s/Terraform/Vault/Istio/TLS/replicas) removed or mapped to stdlib (SQLite, lru_cache, direct calls, logging, pytest). See DESIGN_DECISIONS.md §1.
- Packages mirror components: game/ (Game, state machine Playing⇄Paused→GameOver, scoring), questions/ (Question, answer checking via fractions.Fraction + repository), users/, admin/, ui/.
- State machine raises on invalid transitions; pausing only between answers.
- Answer acceptance: Fraction(input) == Fraction(answer); 2/4 == 1/2.
- Round = 10 questions; 100 pts/correct; stars by percentage (≥50/≥75/≥90).
- Persistence: sql/schema.sql (games, questions, scores); data/questions.json 20+ seed questions (equivalent, compare, add_subtract, simplify).
- UI: ui/theme.py central palette/fonts; every screen a Frame class with a Canvas starfield drawn on <Configure>; App controller has screens dict + show(name); create_app(root) factory; maximized, F11 fullscreen, Esc exit; min 1100x750; no mainloop() in factory.
- tests/ headless domain + state machine + sequences + persistence (temp SQLite) + test_ui_smoke.py (single Tk, retry 3x, show every screen, correct+wrong submission with cleared input).
